themes_detail.label: Street Damage Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 143 THIS WEEK—a 484% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 24.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 13.66)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in road infrastructure across the Upper West Side that demands immediate investigation into root cause and scope.
evidence: 143 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 24.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (484% spike)
Z-score of 13.66 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Coincides with damaged tree spike (11 complaints this week vs. 0.5 avg), suggesting possible weather event or infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: What triggered this sudden wave of street deterioration—weather, deferred maintenance, or construction?
Interview DOT about inspection backlogs and repair timelines on affected streets

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints exploded to 11 THIS WEEK—a 2,100% increase from the 8-week average of 0.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 14.85, highest severity)—indicating a possible weather event or citywide tree health crisis affecting the neighborhood's urban forest.
evidence: 11 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,100% increase)
Highest z-score in dataset (14.85), indicating most statistically anomalous issue
Correlates with street condition spike, suggesting possible severe weather event this week
reporting_angles: Was there a storm or high winds this week that caused branch damage or tree failures?
Interview Parks Department about tree inspection protocols and whether this signals a broader urban forest health problem

themes_detail.label: Traffic Disruption Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints surged to 4 LAST WEEK—a 967% increase from the 8-week average of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 7.49)—representing an unusual surge in traffic congestion or incident reports that warrants investigation into causes and duration.
evidence: 4 traffic complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing suggests possible connection to construction, event, or infrastructure changes
reporting_angles: Were there major road closures, events, or construction projects on the Upper West Side last week?
Interview NYPD Traffic about congestion patterns and whether this was localized to specific avenues

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Stress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints peaked 2 WEEKS AGO at 17—a 656% increase from the 8-week average of 2.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.33)—suggesting possible infrastructure strain or maintenance issues in the neighborhood's underground systems.
evidence: 17 sewer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (656% increase)
Z-score of 6.33 indicates statistically significant anomaly
May correlate with street/tree damage spike if caused by heavy rainfall or weather event
reporting_angles: Did the neighborhood experience flooding or sewer backups 2 weeks ago tied to weather?
Interview DEP about maintenance schedules and whether aging Upper West Side infrastructure is becoming more failure-prone

themes_detail.label: Noise Pollution Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints reached 28 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 122% increase from the 8-week average of 12.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.4)—while park noise spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (500% increase from 0.5 avg, z-score: 3.54), suggesting emerging patterns of outdoor disturbance.
evidence: Vehicle noise: 28 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 12.6 weekly average (122% increase)
Park noise: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase)
Combined signals suggest either temporary event-driven disturbance or behavioral shift in neighborhood use patterns
reporting_angles: Were there major outdoor events, concerts, or gatherings in neighborhood parks last week?
Interview Parks enforcement about whether they've noticed increased vehicle traffic or noise violations near green spaces
